{{Short description|Early form of Newar language}} {{Infobox language | name = Classical Nepal Bhasa | altname = Old Newar | nativename = {{Lang|nwc|पुलाङु नेपाल भास}} | states = [[Nepal]], [[India]], [[Tibet]], [[Bhutan]] | region = | era = Developed into [[Newar language|Modern Nepal Bhasa]] in the 19th century | script = *[[Bhujimol script]] *[[Newar script]] *[[Kutila script]] *[[Ranjana script]] * various [[Nepalese scripts]] | familycolor = Sino-Tibetan | fam2 = [[Newaric languages|Newaric]] | notice = Indic | iso2 = nwc | iso3 = nwc | glotto = none | image = 1374 CE, The Haramekhala medical manual, Newar language, Bhujimol script.jpg | imagecaption =A 14th century palm-leaf manuscript of the Haramekhala, a medical manual written in Classical Newar and the [[Bhujimola script]]. | ancestor = [[Proto-Sino-Tibetan]] | ancestor2 = [[Proto-Tibeto-Burman]]? }} '''Classical Newar''' or '''Classical Nepal Bhasa''' ({{langx|new-Latn|label=[[Newar language|Modern Newar]]|pulāṃ bhāy}}, {{gloss|old language}}) also known as '''Old Newar''', is the vernacular and literary form of [[Nepal Bhasa]] used prior to the 19th century.{{Cite book |last=Malla |first=Kamal Prakash |url=http://archive.org/details/ADictionaryOfClassicalNewariKamalP.Malla |title=A Dictionary of Classical Newari |publisher=Cwasa Pasa |year=2000 |isbn=99933-316-0-0 |location=Kahtmandu, Nepal |pages=vii}} The term is most generally used to describe the form of Nepal Bhasa used in manuscripts and other sources from the [[Malla dynasty (Nepal)|Malla dynasty]].{{cite book|last1=Acharya|first1=Baburam|title=Nepal, Newar and Newari language|date=1952|publisher=Nepal-Sanskritik Parisad|location=Kathmandu, Nepal}}Alan Hopkinson (2008) ''UNIMARC Manual: Bibliographic Format''. Walter de Gruyter. The antiquity of the Newar language is not known. The [[Sanskrit]] stone inscriptions from the [[Licchavis of Nepal|Licchavi Dynasty]] contains frequent use of [[Sino-Tibetan languages|Sino-Tibetan]] words, especially for proper nouns like names of person, settlements and rivers, suggesting the existence of a vernacular [[Sino-Tibetan languages|Sino-Tibetan language]] which is believed to be an early form of the Newar language.''{{Cite book |last=Shrestha |first=Purushottam Lochan |url=https://archive.org/details/TripurRaYuthunimamRajkulPurushottamLochanShrestha |title=Tripura ra Yuthunimama Durbara |publisher=Bhaktapur Offset Prints |year=2001 |isbn=99933-622-0-4 |page=4 |language=ne |trans-title=The Royal Houses of Tripura and Yuthunimama}}''{{Cite book |last1=Levy |first1=Robert Isaac |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ngacsMPGJPcC |title=Mesocosm: Hinduism and the Organization of a Traditional Newar City in Nepal |last2=Rājopādhyāya |first2=Kedar Rāj |date=1990 |publisher=University of California Press |isbn=978-0-520-06911-4 |pages=36 |language=en}} ==History== Classical Newar language was the official language of Nepal from [[Licchavi (kingdom)|Licchavi era]] to [[Malla (Nepal)|Malla era]] of Nepal. ===Licchavi period=== Newar words appeared in [[Sanskrit]] inscriptions in the Kathmandu Valley for the first time in the fifth century. The words are names of places, taxes and merchandise indicating that it already existed as a spoken language during the [[Licchavi (kingdom)|Licchavi]] period (approximately 400–750 AD).Tuladhar, Prem Shanti (2000). ''Nepal Bhasa Sahityaya Itihas: The History of Nepalbhasa Literature.'' Kathmandu: Nepal Bhasa Academy. {{ISBN|99933-56-00-X}}. Pages 19–20. The inscriptions from the [[Licchavi (kingdom)|Licchavi]] period includes Newari words. ===Thakuri period=== The earliest known (dated) document in Nepal Bhasa is called "The Palmleaf from Uku Bahal" which dates back to 1114 AD (235 NS).{{cite news|last=Malla|first=Kamal P|title=The Earliest Dated Document in Newari: The Palmleaf from Uku Bahah NS 234/AD 1114|url=http://www.kpmalla.com/wp-content/uploads/2009/08/kailash_16_0102_02.pdf|accessdate=18 April 2011|newspaper=Kailash|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322213131/http://www.kpmalla.com/wp-content/uploads/2009/08/kailash_16_0102_02.pdf|archive-date=22 March 2012|url-status=dead |pages=15–25}}
{{lang|nwc|छु पुलेंग कीत्य बिपार वस्त्र बिवु मिखा तिवु मदुगुन छु सात दुगुनव ल्है}} {{transliteration|nwc|chīna ḍhākō tr̥saṃghaṣa paribhōga, chu pulēṃga kītya bipāra vastra bivu mikhā tivu maduguna chu sāta dugunava lhai}}
The earliest dated stone inscription in [[Thakuri dynasty]] is in [[Newar language|Newar]], dated [[Nepal Sambat]] 293 (1173 CE).{{cite web |url=http://www.kpmalla.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/11/Classical-Newari-Literature.pdf |title=Classical Newari Literature |date=1981 |last=Malla |first=KP|page=1 |access-date=19 March 2014 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322213147/http://www.kpmalla.com/wp-content/uploads/2010/11/Classical-Newari-Literature.pdf |archive-date=22 March 2012}} ===Malla period=== The earliest important books of Classical Newar from the 14th century are ''Haramekhalā'' (1374), ''[[Manav Nyaya Shastra|Mānava Nyāyaśāstra]]'' (1380), ''Amarkośa'' (1381), and ''[[Gopal Raj Vamshavali|Gopālarāja Vaṃśāvalī]]'' (1389).Tuladhar, Prem Shanti (2000). ''Nepal Bhasa Sahityaya Itihas: History of Nepalbhasa Literature.'' Kathmandu: Nepal Bhasa Academy. {{ISBN|99933-56-00-X}}. Pages 20, 25.Lienhard, Siegfried (1992). ''Songs of Nepal: An Anthology of Nevar Folksongs and Hymns.'' New Delhi: Motilal Banarsidas. {{ISBN|81-208-0963-7}}. Page 1. The language continued growing in the Medieval period and enjoyed royal patronage. Noted royal writers include [[Mahendra Malla|Mahindra Malla]], [[Siddhi Narasimha Malla|Siddhinarsingh Malla]], [[Jagat Prakasha Malla|Jagatprakash Malla]] etc. An example of the language used in that period is provided by lines of Mooldevshashidev written by Jagatprakash Malla which verse describes [[Shiva]] and the use of a tiger skin as his seat. Mooldevshashidev by Jagatprakash Malla, edited by Saraswati Tuladhar{{fcn|date=September 2025}}
